note: Day numbering follows the consecutive count used by Boston 25, NBC Boston, Boston Globe and Fox News (Day 1 = July 27). CBS Boston used a divergent count in at least one headline.

pretrial.event: District Court arraignment via Zoom from a Boston hospital; not guilty plea to three counts each of murder, strangulation, and assault and battery with a dangerous weapon.
Plymouth County grand jury indicts on three counts each of murder and strangulation.

Superior Court arraignment held at Tewksbury State Hospital; not guilty plea; held without bail at the facility. Forensic psychologist Dr. Karin Towers reported continuing depression and suicidal ideation.

Judge Sullivan orders The New Yorker to disclose reporter Eren Orbey's interview materials from his Patrick Clancy profile; subpoena later quashed June 2, 2025 on jurisdictional grounds with leave to reissue in New York. As of Oct 2025, no materials produced.
Prosecutors move to drop strangulation counts as redundant; case proceeds on three counts of first-degree murder.
Jury selection begins; nearly 90 prospective jurors appear on day one.
Jury seated: 18 jurors (12 women, 6 men; 12 deliberating + 6 alternates). Judge Sullivan rules autopsy photos and the father's 911 call audio impounded from public view.

days.headline: Opening statements; Patrick Clancy is the first witness
days.summary: Prosecutor Shanan Buckingham argued Clancy planned the killings, describing searches for takeout and the route between home, a restaurant and CVS, and saying she strangled the children with exercise bands in the basement. Defense attorney Kevin Reddington said Clancy 'is aware that she killed her children and is not trying to deny that' but was suffering postpartum psychosis and was over-prescribed — '13 different psychiatric medications.'

witnesses.name: Patrick Clancy
witnesses.gist: Called as the prosecution's first witness.

days.headline: Patrick Clancy describes the night; jury hears the 911 call
days.summary: Patrick Clancy testified to discovering the children in the basement and finding Lindsay injured outside; the jury heard his ~6-minute 911 call. A CVS manager and a restaurant hostess each described normal interactions with Lindsay that evening.

witnesses.name: Patrick Clancy
witnesses.gist: Described finding the children with exercise bands around their necks and Lindsay outside with cut wrists; recalled her saying 'I tried to kill myself'; the jury heard his 911 call.

witnesses.name: Angela Krause
witnesses.gist: Lindsay's medication call was 'a very normal interaction.'

witnesses.name: Sweeney Schelgren
witnesses.gist: Took the takeout order; no signs of impairment.

days.headline: First responders describe the scene
days.summary: Duxbury police and fire personnel described the response: Clancy found injured outside; CPR performed; children transported.

witnesses.name: Stephen Hall
witnesses.gist: Found Lindsay injured outside; heard Patrick screaming from the basement.

witnesses.name: Brian Josephine
witnesses.gist: Arrived during the initial response.

witnesses.name: PJ Hussey
witnesses.gist: 'It turned very chaotic very quickly.'

witnesses.name: Loring 'Chuck' Nudd
witnesses.gist: Performed CPR; transported Dawson to Plymouth hospital.

witnesses.name: Keith Nette
witnesses.gist: Assisted with chest compressions.

witnesses.name: Patrick Dwyer
witnesses.gist: Part of the response.

witnesses.name: Jennifer Stratton
witnesses.gist: Carried Callan to an ambulance.

witnesses.name: Robert Costanzo
witnesses.gist: Treated Lindsay; administered Narcan; she remained unresponsive.

witnesses.name: Daniel Dougherty
witnesses.gist: Final witnesses of the day.

witnesses.name: Vincent Cahill
witnesses.gist: Final witnesses of the day.

days.headline: Jury views the Duxbury home; ER physicians testify
days.summary: Jurors inspected the home's exterior, basement and both floors, and were driven past ThreeV and the Kingston CVS. ER physicians described treating Dawson and Callan.

witnesses.name: Dr. Mark Tenerowicz
witnesses.gist: Treated Dawson, who arrived without pulse; declared him dead at 7:28 p.m.

witnesses.name: Dr. Benjamin Kaufman
witnesses.gist: Restored Callan's heartbeat but 'at no time did he have any brain function'; transferred to Boston Children's.

witnesses.name: Marcanthony Maffeo
witnesses.gist: Accompanied the sedated Clancy by medical flight to Brigham and Women's.

witnesses.name: Richard Lippard
witnesses.gist: Described Clancy 'sedated, not speaking.'

witnesses.name: Melissa Arcadipane
witnesses.role: Lab tech supervisor, South Shore Hospital
witnesses.gist: Processed blood/urine samples for State Police.

days.headline: The journals read aloud, and the hospitals' account of that night
days.summary: Prosecutor Shanan Buckingham read excerpts from Clancy's journals aloud through Trooper Cory Melo, who seized them in the home search: 'I'm completely overwhelmed trying to take care of the three kids. I feel like I'm drowning every day.' Kevin Reddington read on from the same pages for the defense: 'I don't know what's wrong with me. I want help. I want to be well.' The rest of the day was the medical response: ER and ICU doctors from three hospitals, two Brigham nurses, two hospital psychiatrists who evaluated Clancy while she was intubated, and the troopers who took her blood and searched the house.

witnesses.name: Cory Melo
witnesses.gist: Seized Clancy's journals in the home search; excerpts were read aloud as he testified.

witnesses.name: Capt. John Santos
witnesses.gist: Described executing the search warrant; laptops, exercise bands, a phone and notebooks were seized.

witnesses.name: Sgt. Robert Flynn
witnesses.gist: Described securing the scene and Duxbury's part in the search warrant.

witnesses.name: Det. Mark Farioli
witnesses.gist: Collected Clancy's blood and urine samples for the state lab.

witnesses.name: Trooper Leah O'Connell
witnesses.gist: Received the blood and urine vials taken from Clancy.

witnesses.name: Sgt. Rose Stoffers
witnesses.role: Mass. State Police, crime scene services
witnesses.gist: Photographed and documented Clancy's injuries at the hospital.

witnesses.name: Dr. Jhilam Biswas
witnesses.gist: Evaluated Clancy while she was intubated; she wrote 'horrified' when asked about her mood. Testified she saw no signs of psychosis in that evaluation.

witnesses.name: Dr. Sejal Shah
witnesses.gist: Evaluated whether Clancy could change her health care proxy; described her mood as 'OK' and her thoughts as 'organized.'

witnesses.name: Rachelle Amedee
witnesses.role: Nurse, Brigham and Women's trauma ICU
witnesses.gist: Cared for Clancy after she arrived; documented episodes of delirium and visual hallucinations, and communication by whiteboard.

witnesses.name: Meghan Collins
witnesses.gist: Testified to Clancy's care and recovery in the intensive care unit.

witnesses.name: Dr. Kelly McDonough
witnesses.gist: CT of Clancy's head showed nothing remarkable; she was treated for a thoracic spine injury.

witnesses.name: Dr. Andrew Capraro
witnesses.gist: Described Callan's condition on arrival, including swelling of the brain.

witnesses.name: Dr. David Casavant
witnesses.gist: Described 'an enormous amount of brain swelling' and no response to basic testing.

witnesses.name: Dr. Michael Snyder
witnesses.gist: Treated Cora, who 'was not breathing on her own when she arrived'; declared her dead after resuscitation failed.

days.headline: Toxicology: drugs in Clancy's system, none in the children
days.summary: A surgeon described Clancy's spinal injuries from the fall. State Police testified to finding prescription bottles; eight crime-lab witnesses covered toxicology — prescription drugs detected in Clancy's blood and urine, nothing in the children. The parties stipulated the children's toxicology testing was done correctly. (Date per CBS 'Day 6' label; CBS's own dating was internally inconsistent.)

witnesses.name: Dr. Cristina Karpio
witnesses.gist: Described complex spinal injuries from the second-story fall.

witnesses.name: Lt. Joseph Rabbit
witnesses.gist: Found four prescription bottles in a kitchen cabinet during the search.

days.headline: Toxicology detail, DNA on the exercise bands, the former nanny
days.summary: Analysts detailed benzodiazepines in Clancy's system at largely therapeutic levels; DNA from the exercise bands included Dawson, Callan and Patrick Clancy. The former nanny called Clancy 'a wonderful mom who loved her kids' who had shared she was suffering postpartum issues.

witnesses.name: Eitan Negri
witnesses.gist: Repaired wrist lacerations Jan 25, 2023; neck cuts 'superficial.'

witnesses.name: Nicholas Roberts
witnesses.gist: Detected 'at least four or five' benzodiazepines; no alcohol.

witnesses.name: Dr. Justin Brower
witnesses.gist: One drug 'a little elevated'; the rest therapeutic; not at suicidal levels.

witnesses.name: Katarina Stashyn
witnesses.gist: Mixed DNA profiles on exercise bands; Lindsay's DNA on shingles outside the home.

witnesses.name: Elaine Rossi
witnesses.gist: 'A wonderful mom'; Clancy shared postpartum struggles and sleep difficulties; no concerns about the children's safety.

days.headline: Medical examiner; pediatrician; family and friends
days.summary: The medical examiner who performed the autopsies testified (Callan's cause of death: complications of mechanical asphyxia). The children's pediatrician saw Cora the morning of the deaths in a routine visit and 'never saw signs of postpartum issues' in Lindsay. The former father-in-law described 'an all-American family' and Lindsay's 'blank stare' at Thanksgiving.

witnesses.name: Dr. Kimberly Springer
witnesses.gist: Performed the autopsies; Callan's cause of death 'complications of mechanical asphyxia.'

witnesses.name: Dr. Lindsay Rosshirt
witnesses.gist: Children healthy; examined Cora that morning; saw no postpartum signs in Lindsay.

witnesses.name: Christopher Clancy
witnesses.gist: Devoted mother; 'blank stare' at Thanksgiving; his overnight offer declined; Patrick very concerned for his wife.

witnesses.name: Susan Fraone
witnesses.gist: Dawson had difficult drop-offs starting Oct 2022.

witnesses.name: Susan Bertolo
witnesses.gist: Testified about the day before the deaths.

witnesses.name: Bethany DeCollibus
witnesses.gist: Knew of insomnia; never heard suicidal ideation.

witnesses.name: Andrea Hennigan
witnesses.gist: Texted with Lindsay the day before about medication adjustments.

witnesses.name: Kyle Carney
witnesses.gist: Testified about a Jan 22, 2023 social gathering.

witnesses.name: Det. Sgt. Andrew Chiachio
witnesses.gist: Recovered surveillance footage, DNA samples, search-warrant evidence.

days.headline: Her psychiatrists testify; a hot mic and a warning from the bench
days.summary: Two psychiatrists who treated Clancy testified: Jennifer Tufts, who saw her from September 2022, and Alia Goodheart, from the voluntary inpatient stay at McLean over New Year's. A family friend and the woman who ran the childcare room at the family's club also took the stand. Before the testimony, Kevin Reddington told the court a prosecutor had been caught on a hot mic saying 'shut her up' while Clancy sobbed during Thursday's autopsy testimony. Judge William Sullivan warned that anyone making inappropriate comments would be escorted out and barred from the rest of the trial.

witnesses.name: Dr. Jennifer Tufts
witnesses.gist: Clancy's psychiatrist from September 2022; testified to the appointments and medication changes running to January 23, 2023, and to her reluctance to take medication. Testimony continued Day 10.

witnesses.name: Dr. Alia Goodheart
witnesses.gist: Treated Clancy during the January 1-5, 2023 voluntary admission; testified she reported feeling numb and sleeping badly, denied any plan to harm herself, named her children as reasons to live, and showed no signs of psychosis. 'I had no reason to believe that she was not a reliable reporter.'

witnesses.name: Sarah Carney
witnesses.gist: A college friend of Patrick Clancy; said Clancy looked thinner and more frail by late 2022 but was 'quiet, but fairly normal' at a bonfire two days before the killings.

witnesses.name: Kimberlee Hardy
witnesses.role: Former child services director, Kingsbury Club, Kingston
witnesses.gist: Supervised the two older children in the club playroom; described Clancy as 'very shy' at drop-off and the family as careful about exposing the infant to illness.

days.headline: Tufts: 'no signs of psychosis' the day before the killings
days.summary: Dr. Jennifer Tufts, who treated Clancy across 14 telehealth visits through Jan 23, 2023, said she found no signs of psychosis or mania at the final appointment and that Clancy denied suicidal or homicidal ideation. The defense pressed her limited experience and that she never obtained other providers' records. Nurse practitioner Julie Paul described the November 2022 intake: ideation denied; sleep the main concern.

witnesses.name: Dr. Jennifer Tufts
witnesses.gist: 'No signs of psychosis or mania' Jan 23; Clancy denied suicidal/homicidal ideation but felt 'close to feeling suicidal'; ~10 medications tried; cross highlighted her limited postpartum caseload and missing records.

witnesses.name: Julie Paul
witnesses.role: Psychiatric NP; ex-director, perinatal behavioral health, South Shore Health
witnesses.gist: Nov 22, 2022 screening: ideation denied, no hallucinations/delusions; sleep the main concern; prescribed Prozac 10mg; transferred care Nov 30.

days.headline: Psychiatric nurse: suicidal thoughts documented, 'never thoughts of harming her children'
days.summary: Nurse Rebecca Jollotta testified Clancy had persistent, intrusive suicidal thoughts but — documented repeatedly — never thoughts of harming her children. She suspected possible bipolar disorder; prescribed Seroquel, Valium, Lamictal; expressed reluctance when Clancy asked to taper Seroquel but sent the prescription. Final clinic contact: Patrick's Dec 30 call seeking a McLean bed.

witnesses.name: Rebecca Jollotta
witnesses.role: Psychiatric nurse, South Shore Health perinatal program
witnesses.gist: Persistent suicidal ideation; 'never had thoughts on harming her children'; suspected bipolar; taper reluctance; cross noted records she never received.

days.headline: Counselor's notes; medical examiners on the autopsies
days.summary: Counselor Latiesha Dukes saw Clancy four times in December 2022 — first visit noted 'frequent suicide ideation,' final visit showed improvement; referred to higher-level care. Medical examiners testified on autopsy findings for all three children.

witnesses.name: Sgt. Daniel Lawlor
witnesses.gist: Evidence officer; hospital observation.

witnesses.name: Latiesha Dukes
witnesses.role: Mental health counselor, South Shore perinatal clinic
witnesses.gist: Dec 2: depression symptoms, frequent suicidal ideation → postpartum anxiety diagnosis; Dec 9: improved; referred to Women and Infants.

witnesses.name: Nicole Bradley
witnesses.gist: Hospital watch duty.

witnesses.name: Dr. Renee Stonebridge
witnesses.gist: Autopsy findings for all three children.

witnesses.name: Dr. Barbara Olson
witnesses.gist: External examination of Cora.

days.headline: Digital forensics: the searches and the October note
days.summary: State Police digital forensics presented: an Aug 23, 2022 laptop visit to a suicide-methods page; a Jan 20, 2023 phone search 'Can you treat a sociopath'; an Oct 25, 2022 note beginning 'I'm sad and depressed. I can't parent my 3rd child like my first'; and Jan 23–24 texts and calls. No court Friday Aug 14.

witnesses.name: Sgt. Kyle Pavao
witnesses.gist: Laptop history: suicide-methods page visit Aug 23, 2022.

witnesses.name: Timothy Chiappini
witnesses.gist: Phone extraction: 'Can you treat a sociopath' search (Jan 20, 2023); Oct 25, 2022 note; Jan 23–24 messages.

witnesses.name: Joshua McKelligan
witnesses.gist: Described the bedroom scene and stains on ledge/shingles; Museum of Science surveillance video.

days.headline: Prosecution rests after ~70 witnesses; defense begins
days.summary: Cellebrite expert Ian Whiffin closed the Commonwealth's case with iPhone data from Jan 24, 2023: stair climbs at 5:33 and 5:38 p.m., a final heart-rate reading at 5:23 p.m., and searches including 'ketamine for suicide ideation' (Jan 18) and 'symptoms of postpartum psychosis' (Jan 19). The Commonwealth rested Monday morning. The defense opened with character and family witnesses: nurse colleague Margaret Hamp, sister Allison Ozga, and mother Paula Musgrove — who read an October 2022 text, 'Mom will you please come up and stay with me…Something is wrong,' and said Lindsay disclosed 'thoughts of harming the children' in late December.

witnesses.name: Ian Whiffin
witnesses.gist: Apple Health data; stair climbs 5:33/5:38 p.m.; searches re: ketamine and postpartum psychosis; data stops at 5:38 p.m. per cross.

witnesses.name: Margaret Hamp
witnesses.gist: 'The kind of nurse you want taking care of you'; once called police for a wellness check over a baby-cam concern.

witnesses.name: Allison Ozga
witnesses.gist: Decline from Thanksgiving to Christmas 2022; suicidal thoughts at Christmastime after McLean discharge.

witnesses.name: Paula Musgrove
witnesses.gist: 'Things changed in October'; the 'Something is wrong' text; late-Dec disclosure of thoughts of harming the children; cross: she didn't consider commitment or separation. Also: 'The medication was pretty much just destroying her mind.'

witnesses.name: Michael Vulfovich
witnesses.gist: Reviewed Clancy's Jan 24 injuries.

days.headline: 'She was begging for help'; the psychologist and the voice
days.summary: Former mother-in-law Sue Clancy (a 38-year L&D nurse practitioner) said Lindsay 'was begging for help' in November 2022. Psychiatrist Dr. Donald Condie called the records 'somewhat sparse' and described postpartum psychosis symptoms. Forensic pathologist Dr. Elizabeth Laposata described a 'freefall dive headfirst.' Dr. Paul Zeizel, who had seen Clancy 45+ times, said she reported hearing 'a male voice ordering her' that she 'had no choice but to kill her children. And kill herself.'

witnesses.name: Sue Clancy
witnesses.role: Former mother-in-law; NP, South Shore L&D
witnesses.gist: 'Begging for help' Nov 2022; referred her to the postpartum program; 'very nurturing, very loving, wonderful mother.'

witnesses.name: Dr. Donald Condie
witnesses.gist: Records 'somewhat sparse'; Zoloft increase left her 'numb, not herself'; described postpartum psychosis symptoms.

witnesses.name: Dr. Elizabeth Laposata
witnesses.gist: 'Freefall dive headfirst' causing spinal compression/paralysis; Callan's bruising attributed to medical equipment.

witnesses.name: Dr. Paul Zeizel
witnesses.gist: 45 visits since the incident; she reported a male voice ordering the killings.

days.headline: Zeizel: she could not tell right from wrong; TikTok witness excluded
days.summary: Dr. Zeizel concluded Clancy 'was unable to conform her behavior to the rule of law' and experienced derealization and psychosis in late 2022; she has not heard voices since 2023. Proposed witness Emily Thorndike (a former McLean social worker who posted a TikTok disputing the prosecution's characterization of McLean) was ruled inadmissible for 'limited materiality.' Jury sent home early over an undisclosed 'unforeseen circumstance.'

witnesses.name: Dr. Paul Zeizel
witnesses.gist: ~60 meetings over three years; 'Intrusive thoughts are unrelenting'; opined she could not determine right from wrong on Jan 24, 2023.

witnesses.name: Emily Thorndike
witnesses.gist: Questioned outside the jury; ruled inadmissible — 'limited materiality.'

days.headline: The chaplain and the voice; pink-clad supporters outside
days.summary: Chaplain Sheila Cavanaugh testified Clancy's first words after her breathing tube was removed were 'I am so glad my children are safe,' and that Clancy described a persistent male voice threatening her and the children's safety. On cross, ADA Sprague noted the chaplain's notes never once recorded the voice. Outside, hundreds of pink-clad supporters gathered; Judge Sullivan questioned jurors individually to confirm impartiality. (Outlets differ on her visit count: Globe/WBUR reported 200+; Boston 25 reported at least 14.)

witnesses.name: Sheila Cavanaugh
witnesses.gist: First words after extubation; the reported voice; cross: no note of it in her records.

days.headline: Resnick: 'altruistic filicide.' Defense rests; rebuttal begins with Mack
days.summary: Dr. Phillip Resnick — who testified in the Andrea Yates case — concluded Clancy experienced postpartum psychosis with command hallucinations: 'a puppet and someone else was pulling the strings.' On cross, Sprague cited his own writing that command hallucinations 'are easy to fabricate.' The defense rested (10 witnesses) without calling Clancy. The Commonwealth opened rebuttal with forensic psychiatrist Dr. Avram Mack: major depressive disorder, not psychosis — she 'methodically killed her children one by one' knowing it was wrong. Three rebuttal experts expected in total.

witnesses.name: Dr. Phillip Resnick
witnesses.gist: Evaluated Clancy 4 months after the deaths; postpartum psychosis, command hallucinations, 'altruistic filicide'; cross: his own work says such hallucinations are easy to fabricate.

witnesses.name: Dr. Avram Mack
witnesses.gist: Two April 2026 interviews; major depressive disorder, not psychosis; testified she said 'Go to God' during the killings and could have stopped.

days.headline: Prosecution rebuttal: not psychosis, and a mistrial motion denied
days.summary: The Commonwealth's rebuttal continued. Dr. Avram Mack maintained Clancy had a major depressive disorder rather than psychosis and that psychosis alone would not necessarily prevent someone from knowing right from wrong. Dr. Kirk Heilbrun, a forensic psychologist, told jurors the killings were part of a suicide attempt — that Clancy wanted her children "to be with her so they wouldn't suffer" — called the act out of character, and pointed to inconsistencies in her accounts of hearing a voice. Defense attorney Kevin Reddington moved for a mistrial over Heilbrun's remark that the Catholic Church treats murder as a mortal sin; Judge William Sullivan denied the motion and instructed jurors to disregard the remark as irrelevant.

witnesses.name: Dr. Avram Mack
witnesses.gist: Major depressive disorder, not psychosis; psychosis alone would not necessarily prevent knowing right from wrong.

witnesses.name: Dr. Kirk Heilbrun
witnesses.gist: The killings were part of a suicide attempt; she wanted her children with her; called it out of character and cited inconsistencies in her voice accounts.

days.headline: Heilbrun: 'criminally responsible'; the FBI's Saathoff takes the stand
days.summary: Dr. Kirk Heilbrun concluded that Clancy was criminally responsible for the deaths of her three children. The Commonwealth then called its final rebuttal witness, Dr. Gregory Saathoff, a forensic psychiatrist with the FBI's Behavioral Analysis Unit, who began questioning Clancy's account of her mental state and was still testifying when court adjourned. The judge signaled closing arguments were likely later in the week.

witnesses.name: Dr. Kirk Heilbrun
witnesses.gist: Concluded Clancy was criminally responsible for the deaths of her three children.

witnesses.name: Dr. Gregory Saathoff
witnesses.gist: The state's final rebuttal witness; began challenging her account of her mental state and was still on the stand at day's end.

days.headline: Prosecution rests its rebuttal; closings set for Thursday
days.summary: Dr. Gregory Saathoff, the FBI Behavioral Analysis Unit psychiatrist, finished as the Commonwealth's final rebuttal witness, testifying that Clancy "had the capacity to appreciate right from wrong," that she was "criminally responsible," and that command hallucinations "do not propel an individual to automatically obey them." With that the prosecution rested its rebuttal, closing an evidentiary phase that ran 21 days and 84 witnesses. Judge William Sullivan set closing arguments for Thursday, Aug. 27, after which the case goes to the jury.

witnesses.name: Dr. Gregory Saathoff
witnesses.gist: Final rebuttal witness; testified she could appreciate right from wrong and was criminally responsible, and that command hallucinations do not force a person to act.

days.headline: Closing arguments delivered; jury begins deliberating
days.summary: In closings Thursday, prosecutor Jennifer Sprague argued Clancy planned the killings and knew they were wrong — that she "knew that she would have a limited amount of time" — while telling jurors there was "no dispute" she suffered from mental illness. Defense attorney Kevin Reddington argued she was not criminally responsible, in the grip of postpartum psychosis and failed by inadequate care: "She was reaching out for help and she was not getting it." Judge William Sullivan then gave the case to the jury of nine women and three men; deliberations began about 12:34 p.m. and the panel was excused shortly after 4 p.m., resuming Friday morning.

days.headline: Jury deliberates a second day without a verdict; dismissed until Monday
days.summary: The jury of nine women and three men deliberated for a second day Friday, sending at least one question to the court before Judge William Sullivan dismissed the panel in the afternoon. After more than 10 hours of deliberations over two days it had not reached a verdict, and jurors were told to return Monday, Aug. 31. The judge's instructions give the jury five possible verdicts for the deaths of Cora, Dawson and Callan Clancy — guilty of first-degree murder, guilty of second-degree murder, guilty of manslaughter, not guilty, or not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility — with involuntary manslaughter placed on the slip as a lesser offense after the defense sought it and prosecutors opposed.
